\chapter{Chapter05 — Majority Limits}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter05.MajorityLimits}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Arcsine series coefficient]
\lean{FABL.arcsinSeriesCoefficient}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p136-b007
}
\label{FABL.arcsinSeriesCoefficient}
\leanok
For each natural number $j$, define the arcsine series coefficient by $\displaystyle
\frac{\binom{2j}{j}}{2^{2j}(2j+1)}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Arcsine odd power coefficient]
\lean{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b002
}
\label{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient}
\leanok
For a natural number $k$, the arcsine odd power coefficient is zero when $k$ is even;
when $k$ is odd, it is $\displaystyle \frac{2\binom{k-1}{(k-1)/2}}{k2^k}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Odd-power coefficient identity]
\lean{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient_two_mul_add_one}
\label{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient_two_mul_add_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient, FABL.arcsinSeriesCoefficient}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $j$, the coefficient assigned to the exponent $2j+1$ equals the
arcsine series coefficient with index $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Even-power coefficient vanishing]
\lean{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient_two_mul}
\label{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient_two_mul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $j$, the coefficient assigned to the even exponent $2j$ is
zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Even-index coefficient vanishes]
\lean{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient_mul_two}
\label{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient_mul_two}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient, FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient_two_mul}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $j$, the coefficient of the arcsine power series indexed by
$2j$ is zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Odd-index arcsine coefficient formula]
\lean{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient_mul_two_add_one}
\label{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient_mul_two_add_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient, FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient_two_mul_add_one, FABL.arcsinSeriesCoefficient}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $j$, the coefficient of the arcsine power series indexed by
$2j+1$ equals $\binom{2j}{j}/\bigl(2^{2j}(2j+1)\bigr)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of arcsine coefficients]
\lean{FABL.arcsinSeriesCoefficient_nonneg}
\label{FABL.arcsinSeriesCoefficient_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.arcsinSeriesCoefficient}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $j$, the arcsine series coefficient of index $j$ is
nonnegative.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Half-parameter multichoose coefficient]
\lean{FABL.multichoose_one_half_eq_centralBinom}
\label{FABL.multichoose_one_half_eq_centralBinom}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
For every natural number $n$, the rising-factorial coefficient $\binom{1/2+n-1}{n}$,
interpreted as the generalized binomial coefficient with parameter $1/2$, equals
$\binom{2n}{n}/2^{2n}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of the central binomial ratio]
\lean{FABL.centralBinomialRatio_nonneg}
\label{FABL.centralBinomialRatio_nonneg}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
For every nonnegative integer $j$, the central binomial coefficient divided by $2^{2j}$
is nonnegative: $\displaystyle 0 \le \frac{\binom{2j}{j}}{2^{2j}}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Central binomial coefficient ratio bound]
\lean{FABL.centralBinomialRatio_le_one}
\label{FABL.centralBinomialRatio_le_one}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $j$, the central binomial coefficient satisfies
\[\binom{2j}{j}/2^{2j}\le 1.\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of an arcsine series term]
\lean{FABL.hasDerivAt_arcsinSeriesTerm}
\label{FABL.hasDerivAt_arcsinSeriesTerm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.arcsinSeriesCoefficient}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $j$ and real number $z$, the function $y\\mapsto c_j y^{2j+1}$
is differentiable at $z$ with derivative $\\frac{\\binom{2j}{j}}{2^{2j}}z^{2j}$, where
$c_j=\\frac{\\binom{2j}{j}}{2^{2j}(2j+1)}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Arcsine power series and derivative]
\lean{FABL.arcsinSeries_summable_and_hasDerivAt}
\label{FABL.arcsinSeries_summable_and_hasDerivAt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.arcsinSeriesCoefficient, FABL.centralBinomialRatio_le_one, FABL.centralBinomialRatio_nonneg, FABL.exercise5_18a, FABL.hasDerivAt_arcsinSeriesTerm}
\difficulty{5}
For each integer $j\ge 0$, let $c_j=\binom{2j}{j}/(2^{2j}(2j+1))$. If $z\in\mathbb R$
satisfies $|z|<1$, then the series $\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}c_jz^{2j+1}$ converges, and the
function $y\mapsto\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}c_jy^{2j+1}$ is differentiable at $z$ with
derivative $(1-z^2)^{-1/2}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Odd-power series sum transfer]
\lean{FABL.arcsinOddPowerSeries_hasSum_of_arcsinSeries}
\label{FABL.arcsinOddPowerSeries_hasSum_of_arcsinSeries}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient, FABL.arcsinSeriesCoefficient}
\difficulty{6}
Let $z,a\in\mathbb{R}$. If the series with terms given by the arcsine series coefficient
of index $j$ multiplied by $z^{2j+1}$ has sum $a$, then the series with terms given by
the coefficient of exponent $k$ multiplied by $z^k$ also has sum $a$.
\end{lemma}

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p136-b007}
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $z$ with $|z|<1$, the series
$\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\binom{2j}{j}z^{2j}/2^{2j}$ sums to $(1-z^2)^{-1/2}$. For every
$z\in[-1,1]$, the series $\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\frac{\binom{2j}{j}}{2^{2j}(2j+1)}z^{2j+1}$
and the series with coefficient $0$ at even powers and coefficient
$\frac{2\binom{k-1}{(k-1)/2}}{k2^k}$ at odd powers $z^k$ both sum to $\arcsin z$. At
$z=1$, both series sum to $\pi/2$, and at $z=-1$, both sum to $-\pi/2$.
\end{theorem}
